Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

OncoCohortSelect 0.3.3

  • SelectionOC() and CalibrateThreshold() have a new argument ref.inadmissible for the rule of "br_diff" with admissibility when the reference cohort is not admissible. The default "switch" keeps the rule of the earlier versions: every admissible cohort is a candidate whatever the threshold, which with a threshold of 0 is the two-stage selection of Chakraborty et al. (2026). With "keep", a candidate must exceed the threshold in every trial and the reference cohort is selected without a candidate, so that CalibrateThreshold() always finds a threshold, also when the reference cohort is often not admissible in the null scenario.

OncoCohortSelect 0.3.2

  • The plots name the statistics and the components in words, without underscores. plot() for the results of SimSelection() titles the vertical axis with a short name of the statistic (for example “BR difference” or “Win ratio”) and has a new argument ylab; plot() for the results of SelectionOC() has this name in its default title and labels the selection of no cohort “None admissible”; plot() for the results of BenefitRisk() shows the default labels of the components as, for example, “PFS S(6)” and “OS HR” in its legend. The values returned by the plot methods and the column names of the results are unchanged.
  • The definitions of the components relative to a reference cohort name the reference in words, for example P(rate - reference rate >= 0.1) and P(S(6) - reference S(6) >= 0.05).

OncoCohortSelect 0.3.1

  • The plot() methods have arguments for the colors (col), the sizes of the title, axis titles, axis labels and legend (cex.main, cex.lab, cex.axis, cex.legend) and the position of the legend (legend.position: below the plot by default, above it, inside it or none).
  • Horizontal legends space their entries by the width of each label.

OncoCohortSelect 0.3.0

  • print() and plot() methods for the results of BenefitRisk(), WinStat(), SimSelection() and SelectionOC(), and a print() method for Endpoint(). The results have the classes BenefitRisk, WinStat, SimSelection and SelectionOC; the data frames remain data frames.
  • WinStat() returns the cohorts, the scoring rule and the confidence level in the element settings, and SimSelection() returns the reference cohort, the scoring rule and the confidence level in the attribute settings.
  • The plots use base graphics (packages graphics and grDevices).
  • The example of the article “Posterior benefit-risk score” has larger cohorts and clearer differences between them, and the articles show the new plots.

OncoCohortSelect 0.2.0

Breaking changes

  • SimSelection() compares any number of cohorts with a reference cohort: the arguments treatment and control are replaced by reference and cohorts, and the output has one row per simulated trial and cohort (columns sim, group, is_reference, br, adm, br_diff, br_ref, adm_ref and the win statistics against the reference cohort).
  • SelectionOC() returns the probability of selecting each cohort (columns group and p_select, with a row "(none)" for "br_diff" with admissibility), and CalibrateThreshold() returns p_nonreference, the probability of selecting a cohort other than the reference. In each trial, the cohorts whose statistic exceeds the threshold are candidates and the candidate with the largest statistic is selected.
  • An endpoint used more than once in priority must have decreasing thresholds.

New features

  • Endpoint() accepts columns coded as in ADaM data sets: censor gives a censoring indicator (0 for an event, as CNSR) instead of event, and positive lists the values of a binary endpoint that count as 1 (for example c("CR", "PR") for the best overall response or "Y" for a flag).
  • WinStat() and SimSelection() have the argument scoring: "gehan" (default) or "peron", the scoring rule of Peron et al. (2018) that scores pairs with censored times by the Kaplan-Meier estimates of the cohorts. An endpoint used again with a smaller threshold adds only the pairs decided at the new threshold, as in the BuyseTest package. With "peron", the standard errors treat the Kaplan-Meier estimates as known.
  • Example data of a completed trial with three cohorts in inst/extdata/example_trial.csv.
  • New articles: “Posterior benefit-risk score”, “Net benefit and win ratio”, “Evaluating decision rules by simulation” (three cohorts) and “Analyzing a completed trial”.

Verification

  • Tests of the Peron scoring rule against hand calculations, an independent Python implementation (inst/validation/python/reference.py) and, when it is installed, the BuyseTest package; inst/validation/validate_winstat.R also compares the Peron scoring rule with BuyseTest on simulated trials.

OncoCohortSelect 0.1.0

  • First version.
  • Endpoint() defines binary and time-to-event endpoints; any number of endpoints can be used.
  • PosteriorProb() and BenefitRisk() compute the posterior benefit-risk score of Chakraborty et al. (2026) with beta-binomial models for rates and exponential models with gamma priors for survival probabilities and hazard ratios, against target values or relative to a reference cohort, with admissibility cutoffs and weights.
  • WinStat() computes the net treatment benefit, the win ratio and the win odds of prioritized endpoints with the scoring rule of Gehan, standard errors from the first-order H-decomposition and confidence intervals.
  • SimCohorts() simulates cohorts with correlated progression-free survival, overall survival and response (CorOncoEndpoints) and an independent adverse event; SimSelection(), SelectionOC() and CalibrateThreshold() evaluate selection rules by simulation.
  • Tests against independent Python values, the example of Section S.4 of Chakraborty et al. (2026) and the BuyseTest package; validation scripts in inst/validation and inst/reproduce.
